newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end off highs but undertone firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end off highs but undertone firm.

text.p: Singapore shares ended off their highs on Tuesday on profit-taking but the market undertone remained firm, said dealers.
"There is a bit of profit-taking as prices have run up about 10 to 15 percent in the last two days," said a broker with a Singapore firm.

However, sentiment remained firm ahead of the upcoming budget on Friday and on hopes of a second-half economic pick up led by a recovery in exports, dealers said. "Some overseas funds are have been picking up blue chip heavyweights like the banks and Singapore Press foreign because of the recovery story," said a dealer.
Other gainers included index-linked stocks like Keppel Corp, Fraser & Neave which ended at Singapore $6.80 and S$10.70 respectively.
The key Straits Times Industrial Index ended at 2,007.23, up 9.24 points. Total volume was an active 205.96 million shares with 215 gainers beating 166 losers.
Electronic stocks were also sought after a recent U.S. report showed strong chip sales especially in the Asia Pacific, indicating a recovery in the semiconductor industry.
Several shares touched new highs in intraday trade including Elec & Eltek International at US$6.45, Wong's Circuits at US$1.98 and Serial Systems at S$0.79.
Index-linked NatSteel, which has sizeable electronics interest, gained 24 cents to end at S$4.08 in active volume of over 4.2 million units.
Losers included Thai cellular phone company Total Access Communications which fell 14 cents to end at US$4.84.
Dealers said the sell-off was because of the company's exposure to US-dollar denominated loans.
